primary_antecedent.author: Lars Hörmander
primary_antecedent.title: The Analysis of Linear Partial Differential Operators IV
primary_antecedent.scope: Independent proofs of uniform smooth solvability with only time continuity, the nonvanishing complex coordinate and extension from a parameter slice.

source_correspondence: Boundary barriers and the analytic quotient supplies the two-sided activity, quotient topology and holomorphic factorization. The Hilbert-space operator estimates provide the next analytic tools.

Coefficients are continuous in time with all bounded continuous spatial derivatives. Every pseudodifferential operation is spatial, uniform in the time parameter; no coefficient time derivative or stronger time hypothesis is introduced.

Both signed frequency energies use complete smoothing commutators, with the constant lower-order error independent of the exponential energy weight. Reflection preserves the nonnegative principal coefficient and the low-frequency term is controlled by the exact weak norm.
The support-length Fourier calculation gives the explicit square-root-width bound in every parameter dimension. Absorption yields one strip depending only on the bounded coefficient family.

The exact resolvent commutator has the stated sign and composition order. Global nonnegativity and the bounded Hessian give the square-root gradient bound, and the fractional derivative rearrangement proves the square-root-epsilon energy commutator.

All six fixed-product bounds are proved using complete ordinary conjugation and commutator remainders. The inverse product is an exact finite differential operator; all constants may depend on the already chosen factors, never on the new epsilon.

The cutoff and Jacobi induction includes every commutator and the exact commuting Fourier-multiplier identity. It achieves arbitrary prescribed increasing constants on decreasing strips with a positive common limit.

The exact reflected adjoint has a nonnegative coefficient and the correct complex lower term. The resolvent sequence simultaneously controls the adjoint inequality and the full inverse-product norm of each member of the forcing family.

The forcing recursion uses a valid triangle bound including the full Laplacian increment. The illustrative squared-norm solution retains both the gradient and Laplacian corrections. The zero-forcing case is handled separately.

The infinite product is positive at every finite frequency and decays faster than any power. Dominated norm convergence, full complex Hahn–Banach and Hilbert representation produce a single solution with every spatial derivative; no continuous linear Frechet right inverse is claimed.

Hilbert time traces and spatial Fourier embedding yield joint continuity. The equation gives bounded continuous first time derivatives, including endpoint limits for compactly supported forcing. An explicit two-reflection extension matches both value and derivative.

A uniformly bounded square partition in the inactive parameters removes all support restrictions without differentiating the partition in the equation. Smooth time data yield full smoothness by induction only where those data are smooth.
The exponential equation gives a nowhere vanishing active spatial derivative. The signed finite-integral coordinate solves the homogeneous equation, and the lower-order gauge calculation is exact.

Parameter-slice extension uses globally bounded multipliers. The near-zero Hadamard integral and far-from-zero division are joined with a cutoff, with every derivative bounded. The correcting solutions commute with those multipliers and vanish on the prescribed slice.

component_scope: The coefficient of a Cauchy–Riemann operator may vanish, and its dependence on the distinguished time variable may be only continuous. Nevertheless one can solve the equation with every spatial derivative bounded, uniformly over bounded coefficient and forcing families. The proof uses a half-derivative energy, successively chosen spatial resolvents and a single duality argument in an infinite-weight Hilbert space. It also constructs a homogeneous solution whose derivative in the active spatial direction never vanishes.
